pages.text: Rain fell all morning. Kota couldn't play in the yard and rolled about on the bath porch, bored.
A bull guest looked at the sky from the doorway. He couldn't go to the market, either. Everyone felt gloomy.
Kota pressed their nose to the glass door. It fogged up. "I hate rain. Everything looks blurry."
Dad breathed a misty circle onto the glass and drew with a finger. "Here's a kind of paper for rainy days!"
Kota breathed onto the glass, too, and drew Dad's face.
When the glass cleared, Kota breathed on it again. New white paper! They could draw as often as they liked.
The bull fogged up the next pane and drew a bull carrying a wooden pack frame. "Not bad!" Kota's tail lifted.
Soon the whole glass door became a gallery. Kota, Dad, and the bull drew together. The rain sounded like applause.
Raindrops ran down the glass. "One, breathe! Two, draw! Three, ta-da!" Rainy days became glass-paper days.
Dad hugged Kota from behind by the glass. "A boring day gave us a new game." Kota drew one last circle. "Come again, rain! Breathe out, draw away!"
